Expanded Incircle

GeometryCirclesTriangles
Game: Move the corners of a triangle and slide a point along its bottom side to watch six dots stay on one circle.
How to play: Drag A, B, C or P with a mouse or finger, or focus one with Tab and press the arrow keys. Tick a box to show or hide a guide.
Look for the math

Six dots ride on the sides of a triangle. Slide the starting dot and the other five move with it, yet they always sit on one circle whose centre never leaves the middle of the incircle. Push the starting dot far outside the triangle and the arcs traced by the rotations outline a shape of constant width.

Six equal steps around the triangle

Start at P on BC. Turn the line around corner B until it lands on AB: that gives Q with BQ = BP. Turn around A to get R, around C to get P', then again to get Q' and R'. The tangents from one corner are equal: BD = BF, CE = CD and AE = AF. Subtracting them gives the page's chain FQ = ER = DP' = FQ' = ER' = DP, so the walk closes and CP = CR'. (The page prints AE = EF; the equal pair is AE = AF.)

Why one circle holds all six

The points D, E, F where the incircle touches the sides are exactly halfway along the three equal segments PP', RR' and QQ'. Each segment is at right angles to the radius from the incenter I to its touch point. So every one of the six dots is the same distance from I, and they share a circle centred there. When the starting dot is at D, three turns bring it back to D. The logic test checks all of this on hundreds of triangles and six positions of P. Tick "rotations" to watch the arcs; tick "Gergonne / Adams lines" to see the three lines that meet at the Gergonne point for one special position of P.

Conway's circle and constant width

Let a = BC, b = CA, c = AB and s = (a+b+c)/2. Conway produces each side beyond a corner by the opposite side length, plus the same extra amount x: at B, by b + x. Then DP = s + x and EA' = EC', which puts the six new points on the very same circle in Eves' problem. All three chords PP', QQ', RR' have length 2(s+x) = a+b+c+2x, and each rotated arc has that radius; three such pairs of arcs form a curve of constant width. The page's last paragraph calls the chords (a+b+c)/2 + x; the tests find that this is the half-chord DP, not the chord.

Slide P past B so all six dots lie outside the triangle, then switch on rotations: the orange arcs make a shape you can squeeze between two parallel lines a fixed distance apart. Which two lines touch it there?

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
